Description: End of the Thirty Years' War establishes state sovereignty as the organising principle of international relations.
After Napoleon's defeat European powers redesign the continental order around balance of power.
Britain forces open Chinese markets at gunpoint beginning a century of humiliation.

Japan abolishes the shogunate and industrialises rapidly becoming the first non-Western great power.

European powers partition Africa with borders disregarding ethnic or geographic reality.

Event: Mahan Publishes The Influence of Sea Power
Description: Mahan argues control of the seas determines national greatness inspiring the pre-WWI naval arms race.
Mackinder argues whoever controls the Eurasian Heartland commands the world.
Japan's victory over Russia is the first modern defeat of a European power by an Asian state.
A cascading alliance system pulls Europe into the most destructive war in history to that point.
The Ottoman Empire systematically kills 600000-1.5 million Armenians.
Britain and France secretly carve up the Ottoman Arab territories producing a century of conflict.
The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd creating the first ideological rival to liberal capitalism.
Britain pledges support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
The 600-year empire dissolves leaving a vacuum in the Middle East.
The punitive peace settlement humiliates Germany and plants the seeds of a second world war.
Britain divides the subcontinent into India and Pakistan; up to two million die and Kashmir dispute begins.
Turkey gains control of the Bosphorus and Dardanelles chokepoints.
Germany invades Poland; the conflict kills 70-85 million people and remakes the global order.
44 nations design the post-war financial architecture including the IMF World Bank and dollar system.
Hiroshima and Nagasaki are destroyed beginning the nuclear age and the logic of deterrence.
The UN Charter establishes the Security Council with five permanent veto-wielding members.
Churchill declares an iron curtain has descended across Europe crystallising the Cold War framework.
Kennan's X Article outlines the containment doctrine guiding American strategy for four decades.
The new state survives immediate invasion by five Arab armies as 700000 Palestinians flee or are expelled.
The US pumps $13 billion into rebuilding Western Europe as the Soviet Berlin blockade is broken by airlift.
Twelve nations create the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
Mao Zedong's communist revolution triumphs ending China's century of humiliation.
North Korea invades the South; the first major proxy war kills 2.5 million.
The US and Britain overthrow Iran's elected PM Mossadegh restoring the Shah.
The Korean War ends in stalemate; the 38th Parallel becomes one of the world's most fortified borders.
Dozens of new states gain independence from European colonial powers.
29 African and Asian nations assert non-alignment marking the birth of the Third World movement.
Britain and France seize the Suez Canal; the US forces withdrawal ending European imperial power in the Middle East.
Six nations create the European Economic Community the foundation of the modern EU.
The Soviet Union launches the first satellite beginning the space race.
Fidel Castro takes Havana; Cuba becomes a Soviet client state 90 miles from Florida.
Seventeen African nations gain independence in a single year.
Five oil-producing nations create OPEC to coordinate pricing reshaping global economics.
China and the Soviet Union publicly break over ideology fracturing the Eastern bloc.
The world comes closest to nuclear war during thirteen days of Kennedy-Khrushchev brinkmanship.
Israel defeats Egypt Syria and Jordan capturing the Sinai Gaza West Bank and Golan Heights.
The NPT creates a grand bargain limiting nuclear weapons to five recognised states.
Arab oil producers embargo the West over support for Israel; oil prices quadruple.
The Khmer Rouge takes Phnom Penh; 1.5-2 million Cambodians are killed over four years.
North Vietnamese forces take Saigon ending the Vietnam War after 58000 American deaths.
Ayatollah Khomeini topples the Shah and creates an Islamic republic.
The Red Army enters Afghanistan; the CIA-backed mujahideen resistance eventually produces al-Qaeda.
Saddam Hussein invades Iran; the eight-year war kills up to a million people.
Argentina seizes the Falkland Islands; Britain retakes them in ten weeks.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards help create Hezbollah in the Bekaa Valley.
After eight years and up to one million dead Khomeini accepts a ceasefire.
The Chinese Communist Party crushes pro-democracy protests in Beijing.
East Germans breach the Wall; German reunification and Soviet collapse follow.
A US-led coalition of 700000 troops ejects Iraq from Kuwait in 100 hours.
The Cold War ends; the unipolar moment begins.
The treaty transforms the European Community into the European Union and creates the euro.
Israel and the PLO recognise each other; the peace process begins.
Russia invades Chechnya and is humiliated exposing the post-Soviet military's collapse.
In 100 days Hutu extremists murder approximately 800000 Tutsis.
Nelson Mandela becomes South Africa's first democratically elected president.
The North American Free Trade Agreement links the US Canada and Mexico.
A currency crisis erupts in Thailand and spreads across East Asia.

Description: Both nations conduct nuclear tests within weeks making South Asia a nuclear flashpoint.
The World Trade Organisation replaces the GATT creating the rules-based trade framework.
China fires missiles into waters around Taiwan; the US sends two carrier battle groups.
NATO bombs Serbia for 78 days without UN authorisation to halt ethnic cleansing.
The US transfers control of the Panama Canal to Panama.
China's accession integrates the world's largest labour force into global supply chains.
China Russia and four Central Asian states create the SCO security bloc.
Al-Qaeda strikes New York and Washington killing 2977; the US launches the War on Terror.
Sudan's government backs militia attacks on Black African communities in Darfur; up to 300000 killed.
The US invades Iraq and topples Saddam Hussein unleashing sectarian chaos.
Hezbollah fights Israel to a standstill in a 34-day war enhancing its regional prestige.
Pyongyang detonates a nuclear device despite international pressure.
Russia invades Georgia over South Ossetia and Abkhazia in a preview of the Ukraine conflict.
The collapse of Lehman Brothers triggers the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.
World leaders fail to agree on binding emissions targets previewing US-China climate standoffs.
The US-Israeli Stuxnet virus that damaged Iranian nuclear centrifuges is publicly exposed.
A Tunisian street vendor's self-immolation triggers uprisings toppling regimes across the Arab world.
Xi Jinping announces China's massive infrastructure programme across Eurasia and Africa.
Russian forces seize Crimea from Ukraine fracturing the post-Cold War European security order.
The Islamic State seizes Mosul and declares a caliphate across Syria and Iraq.
Iran agrees to limit its nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief.
Russian air power saves the Assad regime marking Moscow's return to the Middle East.
195 nations agree to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees C tying climate policy to geopolitics.
Britain votes to leave the European Union the most significant rupture in European integration.
An international tribunal rules China's South China Sea claims have no legal basis; Beijing rejects it.
The US Japan India and Australia resurrect the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue.
Washington imposes tariffs on $250 billion of Chinese goods; Beijing retaliates.
The General Data Protection Regulation sets the global standard for data privacy.
Trump reimposes maximum pressure sanctions on Iran accelerating the path to confrontation.
The US recognises Guaido and imposes sweeping sanctions on Maduro's government.
A global pandemic paralyses supply chains and hardens the US-China rivalry into economic decoupling.
Israel normalises relations with the UAE and Bahrain breaking the prior Arab consensus.

The Afghan government collapses as US forces withdraw; the Taliban return to power.

Yevgeny Prigozhin leads an armed march on Moscow before standing down exposing Putin's fragility.

China brokers restoration of Saudi-Iranian diplomatic relations.
Hamas kills 1200 Israelis in a surprise assault; Israel's response devastates Gaza.
BRICS nations announce expanded local-currency trade settlements bypassing the dollar.
Iran Egypt Ethiopia and UAE formally join BRICS representing 46% of world population.

Israel kills Hezbollah's Secretary-General Nasrallah and dismantles its leadership.
Donald Trump's return signals a sharp turn in American foreign policy.
